setupRemoteAddFooterVia: Two ways to connect. Through the phone’s Debian: uses the keys and config in ~/.ssh there (aliases, jump hosts) with no extra public key on the device, but each command takes about 50 ms longer and the phone runs two more ssh processes. Zeta direct: needs no root or Debian and costs less, but first add the public key below to that device. With Debian available it is the default; you can change it on the device page later. The device must run Linux on arm64 or x86-64 with Claude Code installed. Conversations are hosted there and keep running if the phone goes offline or Zeta is closed; you pick them up when you reconnect.
setupRemoteAddFooterDirect: No usable Debian on the phone, so only Zeta direct works: add the public key below to that device, then enter its address. The device must run Linux on arm64 or x86-64 with Claude Code installed. Conversations are hosted there and keep running if the phone goes offline or Zeta is closed; you pick them up when you reconnect.
setupRemoteKeyFooter: Zeta signs in with this key when connecting directly: copy the public key line and add it to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on that device. The private key stays in the phone’s keystore and cannot be exported. The host fingerprint is recorded when you add a device, and only that one is trusted afterwards.

setupRemoteDisconnectBusy: A conversation is active on this device (replying, waiting for your approval, or running background tasks). After you disconnect it keeps running there and you can follow it once you reconnect; requests waiting for your approval can only be answered after reconnecting.

thirdPartyXTextNote: Text encoding library maintained by the Go team. zeta-helper uses it to read GB18030 text. Statically linked into assets/zeta-helper/linux-arm64 and linux-amd64.
thirdPartyClaudeSwitchNote: Switches Claude Code between several Claude accounts; the Accounts page uses it. Built unmodified as a separate program from the tool line in helper/go.mod, packed into assets/claude-switch/linux-arm64 and linux-amd64, and installed on the Linux side on first use; its account package, which identifies the account, is also statically linked into assets/zeta-helper/linux-arm64 and linux-amd64.
thirdPartyAgentUsageNote: Tool that tallies Claude Code usage per account and estimates the weekly quota. zeta-helper links only its reading package (unmodified) to record each weekly quota reading it receives into agent-usage's data directory on the Linux side. Statically linked into assets/zeta-helper/linux-arm64 and linux-amd64.
thirdPartyXCryptoNote: Cryptography library maintained by the Go team. zeta-ssh uses its SSH client to connect to remote hosts directly (key exchange, host signature checks, channels). Statically linked into lib/arm64-v8a/libzeta_ssh.so.
thirdPartyEtaNote: Zeta's Markdown rendering (ui/markdown), sidebar skeleton, adaptive page layout, monospace font definitions, dialog interfaces, the assistant's floating window and the scheduled-task time wheels were copied from Eta and rewritten, used under GPL-3.0; so Zeta is also released under GPL-3.0.
thirdPartyCouiNote: The long-press menu gesture handling (open the menu only after a still press for the full long-press timeout, without swallowing ordinary taps) was copied from COUI 2 and rewritten; used under Apache-2.0.
thirdPartyJetBrainsMonoNote: Monospace font for code, commands and logs (the no-ligature Regular and Bold), unmodified.
thirdPartyKatexNote: Fonts RaTeX {version} uses to typeset formulas, packed into assets/fonts/ with its AAR ({count} KaTeX_*.ttf files), unmodified.
thirdPartyRatexRust: Rust code in the RaTeX native library
thirdPartyRatexRustNote: The Rust standard library and crates statically linked into RaTeX's native library lib/arm64-v8a/libratex_ffi.so (RaTeX's own code is under RaTeX Android).
thirdPartyGoStdNote: zeta-helper and claude-switch are Go programs, each built for linux arm64 and amd64 and packed into assets/zeta-helper/ and assets/claude-switch/; so is zeta-ssh, which connects to remote hosts directly, built for android/arm64 into lib/arm64-v8a/libzeta_ssh.so. All statically link the Go standard library and runtime.

setupImageSummaryIdle: How Debian is stored, its size and checks
setupImageSummaryOff: Not used. Converting speeds up phone boot.
setupImageNoneFooter: Once Zeta's own Debian is installed, its disk image is managed here.
setupImageFooter: The image is a sparse file: the limit reserves nothing, and it only takes as much space as Debian uses. Each boot checks and mounts it, then frees space once.
setupImageMaintainFooter: Resizing and checking first stop everything running in Debian (Claude Code, the SSH server and so on) and start it again afterwards.
setupImageChatRunning: A conversation is running. Resizing and checking need Debian stopped, so wait until it ends.
setupImageTrimSummary: Give the space of files deleted in Debian back to the phone. Debian keeps running.
setupImageResizeSummary: Change the size limit. Stops Debian.
setupImageResizeHint: Enter the new limit in GB. It can't be smaller than the {used} Debian uses. The phone has {free} free. Everything in Debian is stopped first and started again afterwards.
setupImageCheckSummary: Fully check the file system. Stops Debian.
setupImageCheckTitle: Check and repair the disk image?
setupImageCheckConfirm: Everything in Debian, including Claude Code and the SSH server, is stopped first and started again after the check. This usually takes a minute or two.
setupImageDeleteOldSummary: It still takes space and slows down boot. Delete it once Debian works fine.
setupImageDeleteOldConfirm: After deleting it you can't go back to how things were before the conversion. Debian keeps running.
setupImageConvertSummary: On every boot Android rechecks the security label of each file in plain directories. Debian has hundreds of thousands of files, which can add ten seconds or more to boot. In an image it counts as one file.
setupImageConvertFooter: Everything in Debian is stopped first and started again afterwards. Copying temporarily takes as much extra space as Debian uses. The old directory is kept as a fallback; delete it on this page once everything works.
setupImageConvertHint: Enter the size limit in GB. The image is sparse, so the limit reserves nothing. The phone has {free} free.
setupImageInterrupted: It was interrupted halfway (for example by a restart). You can run it again.
setupImageResultConverted: Converted. The old directory is kept as a fallback; delete it on this page once Debian works, so boot gets faster.
setupImageResultResized: The size limit is now {size} GB
setupImageStepFinishSummary: Mount the image, write the boot script, start Debian
setupImageMeasureHint: Can take a minute or two with many files
